research_question: Does a later Qing explanatory recension explicitly distinguish 820-per-limit time/degree conversion from original Ming Xu-An juan45 疾-specific 捷法, and are public print copies available for independent glyph review?

received_locus.work: 秦蕙田《五禮通考》卷一百八十九《嘉禮·觀象授時》, 梅氏文鼎曰
received_locus.explanatory_content: Received text describes an 820 unit as one lunar limit, and expresses conversion from combined solar/lunar angular adjustment to timing by multiplying by 820 and dividing by per-limit lunar motion (遲疾行度). This is a later received explanation of conversion dimensions, not original Xu-An/G893 target glyph or proof of the independent origin or construction of 疾捷法.
received_locus.source_scope: Qing later anthology explicitly attributes the discussion to 梅文鼎; this cannot be counted as a separate early Ming numerical witness nor a new independent Mei authorial autograph.
